title: pr-172345-add-benchmark-lab-multi-variant-reporting-and-profiling-pipeline-v55
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add multi-variant reporting pipeline and profiling baselines; introduces representative workload runners for mixed-traffic and priority-steering scenarios; updates dashboards and alerting to surface regression signals.
commits: Initial commit: add multi-variant runners and reporting pipeline
Add profiling baselines and upload helpers
CI: add reporting pipeline smoke tests
Docs: update README and dashboard links
Fix: tighten metrics tagging for throughput buckets
description: Context: The benchmark lab currently runs single-variant workloads and has limited visibility into multi-tenant/mixed-traffic behavior. This PR adds a multi-variant reporting pipeline (v55) and associated profiling baselines so we can surface regressions that only appear under mixed load and priority-steering scenarios. Motivation: Customers running Dedicated and Private modes report occasional tail-latency regressions when workload mixes change. Our single-variant baselines missed these. Deliverables: 1) representative workload runners that can emit weighted mixes of request profiles (latency-sensitive, throughput-focused, background batch) with configurable priority/weighting; 2) profiling baseline artifacts (v55) stored alongside existing baselines; 3) a reporting pipeline that aggregates run results, computes per-variant percentiles, and writes summary rows to BigQuery/S3; 4) CI smoke tests and an observability dashboard update that surfaces cross-variant regressions. Checklist: - [x] Add multi_variant_runner.py with pluggable profile weights and KV cache warmup support - [x] Add v55_baseline.json with canonical percentiles for representative models - [x] Implement reporting_v55.yaml pipeline + trace_uploader for artifact collection - [x] Add CI job to run a lightweight mixed-workload smoke test on PRs - [x] Update dashboard and alert rules to include variant-delta signals - [x] Add docs and runbook snippets for interpreting multi-variant results Implementation notes: The runner uses the existing benchmark-lab runner interface; new features include request weighting, simulated priority preemption, and optional KV-warmup headers to minimize cold-start noise. The reporting pipeline reuses the reporting library and introduces a new step to compute per-variant deltas and normalized cost-per-token. Baselines were computed from a 2-week controlled run against Dedicated pools and validated with three independent runs. Review conversation snapshot: Miguel Torres (reviewer): "Nice decomposition. Two requests: 1) Can we add a histogram bucket tag for priority level so SLO aggregation can slice by priority? 2) CI flake: the smoke test sometimes times out on small GHA runners." Aisha Patel (author): "Addressed both: added priority_level tag across runners and shortened smoke test runtime + made retries deterministic. Updated CI job to run on a dedicated self-hosted label for reliability." Ravi Singh (reviewer): "Left one comment on trace uploader error handling; otherwise LGTM." Hannah Lee (approver): "Approving — baseline and reporting pipeline look reasonable. Please monitor first 48h of runs after merge." CI summary: All CI checks passed on the final push after fixing flake. Added a GHA job 'benchmark_lab:smoke-mixed' and a scheduled nightly job to recompute baselines. Migration/ops notes: After merge, runbook owners should schedule a baseline recompute if Dedicated pool sizes change by >10%. The reporting pipeline is backwards compatible with v54 artifacts. Rollout: merged to main via squash; dashboards and alerts updated with migration PR. Related: ENG-2187 (benchmark lab multi-variant support), ENG-3301 (profiling baselines automation), SUP-4123 (customer report that triggered investigation).
notes: Post-merge: Nightly recompute scheduled, operations to watch: dashboard alert E2E latency-delta, cost-per-token regressions. Owners: benchmark-lab team (aisha.patel@redwood.ai)
